headline: Augmenting protein language models with structure, dynamics, and graph-based inputs
label: Protein Language Model Prediction
summary: Recent work pairs pretrained protein language model embeddings with structural and dynamics data for function and binding prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is augmenting pretrained protein language model representations with complementary information. DPLM aligns ESM2 sequence embeddings with ViViT-encoded molecular dynamics contact-map trajectories via dual-view contrastive learning, and ProteinJEPA adds a latent-prediction cosine loss to masked language modeling for ESM2 and ProGen3. Other items fuse PLM embeddings with structural descriptors or graph inputs: CLABP aligns ProtT5 embeddings with structural descriptors for antibacterial peptide prediction, SSAS-GO fuses sequence motifs with graph-encoded structure for Gene Ontology annotation, and KSDiffusion pairs an ESM-2 encoder with supervised contrastive learning and conditional diffusion for kinase-specific phosphorylation sites. What is new here is dynamics-level supervision and latent objectives that act on the representation itself rather than on added inputs. Not all items share this route: BERT-T6 fine-tunes ProtBert for T6SS effector identification, and SCOPE trains a Siamese MLP over embeddings for operon pairs, reporting ROC-AUC 0.71.
